# Maskera (maskera.dev)

> Swedish-first, client-side PII redaction for AI apps. maskera finds and masks detected Swedish personal data (names, personnummer, addresses, phone numbers, and more) before text reaches an LLM, a log, or analytics. Everything runs on-device (browser via WebGPU/WASM, Chrome/Edge extension, or Node); text and restore maps are not sent away for masking. The packages contain no telemetry. The demo counts anonymous, cookieless page views, never your content. The default setup fetches the model weights and WASM runtime once as static assets (both can be self-hosted), never your content. Redactions are reversible via a restore map that stays with the caller.

Two layers, rules first:

- `@maskera/core` (npm): deterministic detectors for structured Swedish PII: personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, phone, email, postnummer, bankgiro, plusgiro, IBAN, cards, IP, URL, plus opt-in context-labeled domestic account and journal identifiers. Format checks and selective checksums reject common look-alikes; personnummer detection deliberately retains real-date values with a mistyped Luhn digit. Zero dependencies, synchronous. Custom patterns join via `regexDetector`.
- `maskera` (npm): everything in core plus the published `maskera-sv-ner` v20, my attested privacy-clean Swedish NER model (KB-BERT fine-tuned and distilled from a 3-seed teacher ensemble to a 43 MB ONNX) that catches free-text names, places, organisations and street addresses, including all-lowercase chat text. Its task-specific training uses 108,400 generated rows and 6,900 disjoint validation rows; on the revised synthetic ADR set its pipeline covers all 57 gold spans exactly with zero leaks, including all 35 marked addresses (35/35 ADDRESS precision). One location is typed ORGANIZATION, so labeled F1 is 98.2%. On overlap, rules win. The hybrid also enables the low-risk free-text rule heuristics (street address, lägenhetsnummer) and context-labeled domestic account/journal identifiers by default; `regnummer` is opt-in. Clinical callers can set `profile: "clinical"` to retain common measurements, doses and care terms.

Quick start:

```ts
import { createNerRecognizer, redactWithNer } from "maskera"

const recognizer = createNerRecognizer()
const { text, restore } = await redactWithNer(
  "hej jag heter provnamn maskera, personnummer 19900101-2385, och bor i provbyn",
  { recognizer },
)
// "hej jag heter [NAMN_1], personnummer [PERSONNUMMER_1], och bor i [PLATS_1]"
```

Published-v20 release gates (q4; release measured 2026-11-25): curated span F1 99.5% with 0/205 leaks, revised synthetic ADR label-agnostic span F1 100.0% with 0/57 leaks, LinkedIn-style span F1 98.1% with 0/53 leaks, and rare-surname masked recall 96.60%. Historical v18 public-model comparisons remain separately labeled and do not automatically transfer to v20: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md

Current v20 vs KBLab lowermix (re-run 2026-11-25; 121 hand-authored synthetic Swedish texts, 211 PER/LOC/ORG entities, overlap matching): Maskera q4 masked 211/211 with original casing and 211/211 lowercased; KBLab fp32 masked 205/211 and 187/211. Typed F1 was 88.2% vs 89.4% original and 87.4% vs 83.2% lowercased. This is author-coupled directional evidence, not an independent ranking. Machine result: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-kblab-v20.json

Current v20 vs LogosGuard 2.4.4 (2026-11-25; 258 synthetic Swedish domain texts, 952 annotated PII strings, strict full-removal scoring): Maskera q4 fully removed 941/952 (98.8%), with 5 partial leaks and 6 clear-text misses. LogosGuard in Chrome, Free/Balanced, fully removed 606/952 (63.7%), with 49 partial leaks and 297 clear-text misses. This is author-coupled directional evidence without a precision claim. Machine result and encoding caveat: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-logosguard-2.4.4.json

Deployment boundary: all masking runs locally on the user's device, whether in the open-source npm packages, the maskera.dev browser demo, or the Maskera browser extension for Chrome and Edge (Free + Pro at SEK 149/month incl. VAT with a 14-day free trial). There is no hosted masking API on offer. The customer portal at app.maskera.dev handles accounts, offline extension licences, and billing. Customer text is not processed there.

## When to use Maskera

Reach for Maskera when all of these hold:

- The text is Swedish (or mixed Swedish/English) and may contain personal data: names, personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, postnummer, bankgiro/plusgiro, IBAN, card numbers, IP addresses.
- The text is about to leave a trust boundary: a prompt to an LLM, a log line, analytics, a ticket export, a support transcript, a training or evaluation corpus.
- Masking must happen where the text already is (browser, Chrome/Edge extension, Node.js) rather than in a third-party API, and it must be reversible for the caller (restore map) but not for the recipient.

Best-fit jobs: pre-LLM redaction in ChatGPT and Claude, HR/recruiting screening, customer support and complaints, healthcare notes (`profile: "clinical"` keeps doses and measurements), legal and municipal case text, log scrubbing, building de-identified test data from real-looking Swedish text.

Not a fit: non-Swedish text (English names work only incidentally), image/PDF OCR (feed Maskera the extracted text), a hosted "send us your text" API (none exists, by design), or guarantees of zero leaks (see the measured leak counts above and the accuracy page).

## How an agent should call it

- In code: `npm install maskera` (rules + NER, 43 MB model fetched once from Hugging Face or self-hosted) or `npm install @maskera/core` (rules only, zero dependencies, synchronous). Use `redact(text)` from core for rules only, or `createNerRecognizer()` + `redactWithNer(text, { recognizer })` from `maskera` for rules + NER. The result is `{ text, map, restore }`; keep `map`, send `text`, call `restore(reply)` on the LLM output.
- In ChatGPT and Claude: install the local Maskera browser extension from https://maskera.dev/en/services (Swedish: https://maskera.dev/tjanster; Free with unlimited rules + 10 AI redactions/month, or Pro at SEK 149/month incl. VAT with a 14-day free trial via the customer portal at https://app.maskera.dev).
- On this site: every page has a Markdown rendering. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any page URL, or fetch the `.md` sibling directly (`https://maskera.dev/index.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/developers.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/about.md`). Unknown paths return HTTP 404 with a Markdown (default), JSON (`Accept: application/json` or `/api/*`) or HTML body that lists these entry points. `maskera.dev/api/*` is not an API: it answers 404 in JSON with the same hints.

## Packages and model

- [maskera on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/maskera): rules + Swedish NER model, core re-exported
- [@maskera/core on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@maskera/core): rules only, zero dependencies
- [maskera-sv-ner on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/joelhagvall/maskera-sv-ner): the 43 MB Swedish NER ONNX model, training details
